A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inner Product Transform research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original ShapeNet reconstruction, generation, compression, interpolation, and inversion experiments, including loss and parameter ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical experiments and reports revised reconstruction and generation results alongside the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The IPT definition and two-stage generation pipeline remain. Appendix E revises the neural architectures: the IP-Encoder uses three SiLU convolutional blocks followed by a convolution, while the VAE changes encoder normalization and activations, adds a convolution, and reduces its decoder from five blocks to four.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ShapeNet airplane, chair, and car coverage for reconstruction, generation, compression/upsampling, direct inversion, and interpolation. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LION to reconstruction, where it becomes the strongest comparator; previously it appeared only in generation comparisons. Table 4 adds Point Straight Flows and XCube with 1-NNA results. These additions materially broaden both principal comparisons.

E3.justification: Reconstruction settings change from 256×256 IPTs and 200 epochs to 128×128 IPTs and 5,000 epochs. VAE latent dimensions change from class-specific 32/64/150 to 64 throughout, and cosine annealing of beta is replaced by fixed beta=0.0001. These are substantial reported configuration and training-budget revisions.

E4.justification: The loss ablation in Table 2 and inversion resolution/scale analysis in Table C.1 retain their settings and results. The interpolation case study is retained as Figure C.4, and the point-cloud illustrations reuse existing image content.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and C.1 retain their existing plus/minus reporting practice. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval construction, or significance tests; additional baseline cells do not introduce a new practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces IP-Encoder EMD results for airplanes/chairs/cars from 1.44/8.44/4.16 to 1.57/6.19/3.18, with LION now ranking first. Table 4 replaces the IP-VAE results and adds comparator results. Reported full-pipeline training time changes from about 45 minutes to 8 hours. These results accompany changed settings and do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix F revises the existing injectivity proof: n+1 linearly independent directions become affinely independent directions, a general-position assumption is added, and the threshold argument is revised. v2 already attempted an n+1-direction argument; the other lemmas and surjectivity proof remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract remains unchanged, but the first contribution now emphasizes fast generation while retaining quality rather than matching or exceeding state-of-the-art quality. Section 5 replaces the best-reconstruction claim with qualified comparability to more complex models, narrowing the performance promise.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes theoretical IPT guarantees from empirical behavior of dIPT more explicitly. Section 5 adds a substantive diversity limitation, interpreting middling COV and 1-NNA performance as insufficient VAE expressiveness, and removes the assurance that problematic directions have measure zero.

D1.justification: Appendix E updates tensor shapes and layer-by-layer specifications. Training-time disclosures change from 25 minutes to 2 hours for the encoder and 10–15 minutes to 6 hours for the VAE. Section 4 removes the description of centering, scaling, and bounding-sphere radii; this removal does not establish changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for XCube, Point Straight Flows, and Diss-l-ECT, and removes Gretton et al. while attributing MMD to the already-cited Achlioptas et al. It also emphasizes finite-direction reconstruction for point clouds relative to prior simplicial-complex results. Most research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order are retained. Targeted edits clarify IPT/dIPT terminology, revise contribution and limitation paragraphs, streamline explanations, update affiliations, and replace author-year citations with numbered citations. MMD is relabeled from maximum mean discrepancy to minimum matching distance.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and repositioning of tables and figures. Figure 4 moves to Appendix C as Figure C.4; the redundant main-text downsampling Figure 3 is removed while the fuller Figure B.2 remains. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added LION comparison and revised discussion better calibrate performance claims, while the diversity limitation improves transparency. However, Table 5 retains old reconstruction-reference values despite the revised Table 1, and Section 4.2 still specifies BatchNorm/LeakyReLU where revised Appendix E specifies LayerNorm/ReLU. These inconsistencies obscure the revised experiments' interpretation and reproducibility, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
